gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2's '1,500 W Power Lifting' works by lowering the output voltage and only suits simple resistive loads such as kettles and hair dryers, so anything with a motor or sensitive electronics is still limited by the 600 W inverter. The Technology Man overloaded the unit with a 450 W air duster that pulled over 10 A at startup.
standout_why: I compared against Dealectric's own cited page (dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-under-500), powersized.com/solar-generator-kits/ and offgridempire.com/best-solar-generator-under-500/. Our page prints '600 W (1,500 W Power Lifting)' without saying what Power Lifting does. PowerSized gives only a 100 W solar input limit for the Jackery 300 v2 and lists voltage, current, surge and connector as not listed. OffGridEmpire has no input-limit, surge-mode or compatibility content. None of them says that Power Lifting is for resistive loads only, that the Elite 30 V2 rejects panels whose open-circuit voltage is above 28 V, or that Jackery's own store calls the SolarSaga 100 Air incompatible with the Explorer 300 v2. In the saved chats ChatGPT picked the Elite 30 V2 because its '600W inverter is more versatile', without this caveat. I could not open solargenadvisor.com because of a TLS certificate error, so it is not in this comparison.
decides: This confirms the Elite 30 V2 + 100 W ($489.99 on BLUETTI US today) as the pick, with a scope limit. Its real advantage over the 300 W Jackery, Anker C300 and Elite 30 mini kits is the 600 W rated output. The 1,500 W figure only helps resistive heating loads, run at reduced voltage. It does not help motor startup surges, and a named reviewer overloaded it with a 450 W motor load. Shoppers who need to run a fridge or anything with a motor should be pointed to the 1,024 Wh / 1,800 W ALLPOWERS P1800 kit. The 12–28 V input window (no panels above 28 V open-circuit voltage) means a second panel can't be added in series. Reaching the 200 W input BLUETTI's charge times assume means wiring panels in parallel or buying a 200 W panel. On the Jackery 300 kits, Jackery's own store says the new SolarSaga 100 Air can't recharge the Explorer 300 v2 or Explorer 300, so 'upgrade the 40 W panel later' doesn't work with that panel.

findings.label: Motor-load overload, measured
findings.value: A 450 W mains air duster overloaded the unit; startup current over 10 A, about 2,300 W at switch-on. It ran only with Power Lifting enabled.
findings.source_title: This £189 BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 power station is better than I expected - The Technology Man
findings.note: Clamp-meter reading by Gidon. 10 A × 230 V ≈ 2,300 W. At 120 V the same motor would draw about 19 A at startup for the same wattage; that conversion is my arithmetic, not his measurement.

findings.label: Power Lifting load type, second reviewer
findings.value: 'up to 1500W of pure, restrictive [resistive] power load', for example an electric kettle or hair dryer
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Portable Power Station Review - CGMagazine
findings.note: Matt Keith, 2025-07-31. This is his description of the feature; he reports no measured Power Lifting test.

findings.label: Solar input voltage window (user manual V3.0)
findings.value: 12–28 V; 'Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 28V.'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI ELITE 30 V2 Portable Power Station 600W user manual (V3.0) - ManualsFile
findings.note: This is a third-party copy of BLUETTI's manual; the official PDF on BLUETTI's CDN was too large to read. A 28 V ceiling means two typical 12 V-class 100 W panels in series would exceed it, so a second panel must be wired in parallel. That inference is mine; the manual excerpt I read gives no series/parallel guidance.

findings.label: Solar input reaches 200 W, bench test
findings.value: 200 W reached with a bench power supply simulating ideal sun; no real-sun wattage reported (winter)
findings.source_title: This £189 BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 power station is better than I expected - The Technology Man
findings.note: He used BLUETTI's PV200 200 W panel outdoors. The bundled 100 W panel can deliver at most half of that 200 W input, which is why our page estimates about 4 h rather than BLUETTI's 2.2 h.
